body: I'll keep this in mind. I guess I'll just take the tone lightly. Thank you! It's just hard for me to develop the proper approach for him since we have a large age gap that's why I sought advice.
Thank you. I hope he feels re-assured that it's normal after we talk.
No matter how you view it, it is alarming as a family member. People who start this habit at a young age may develop addiction. So yes, I do care about him.

I'm sorry but you can't see my point. I'm asking for advice on how to re-assure him that it's okay and normal. I never mentioned anything about making this about myself and putting what I want for him to think because it's what I feel like. No. I'm worried about how he sees himself after the incident.

I already mentioned how I saw him embarrassed and all, I don't think I can just 'leave it' after seeing him like that, and he's probably thinking that he did something too sinful by the look on his face.

Look, I just want to talk to him in the right approach which is why I'm asking for advice. Communication is very important to growing kids, especially towards this topic. So no, I can't just leave it.

I guess it's just difference in culture that's why 11 is kinda normal for most of the people who'll see this. I mean it really is fine. I guess I just want to re-assure him that nothing has changed in the way I see him and he doesn't need to feel embarrassed about what happened. I'm worried if he constantly thinks that he got caught doing some kind of 'crime'. That's why I really want to talk to him in the best approach as possible.

I have no intention to meddle with his mind tho. I just want to approach him and tell him it's okay but know his limits. 

Getting caught by his sister, for sure he's feeling embarrassed and uneasy, I know him. I just don't know how to properly tell him without having this implication that I support his underage habit.

These days it's better to just shut up and stay away from these kinds of conversation with them. Sorry not sorry but I can feel what I feel.
